# **Project Summary** {#chapter-1:-overview}

PatientPath is a Digital Medical Referral Network designed for the University of Jordan. It replaces the current paper-based referral process between the Student Clinic and the Jordan University Hospital with an electronic system. The platform allows clinic doctors to create and send referrals digitally, hospital doctors to receive and respond to them, and students to track their referral status. It also integrates the laboratory and pharmacy for managing test results and prescriptions, and connects with the Student Registration Portal to retrieve student information automatically.

# 

# **Chapter 1: Overview** {#chapter-1:-overview}

## **1.0 overview** {#1.0-overview}

PatientPath is a **web-based Digital Medical Referral Network designed for the University of Jordan.** The system digitizes the medical referral process between the University Student Clinic and the Jordan University Hospital.

Currently, when a student visits the Student Clinic and needs specialist care, the clinic issues a paper referral that the student must physically carry to the hospital. This manual process causes several problems: referral papers can be lost or damaged, students experience delays in receiving care, the clinic cannot track whether referred students actually received treatment, and medical records are scattered across departments with no shared access.

PatientPath solves these problems by allowing clinic doctors to create and send referrals electronically, hospital doctors to receive and respond to them in real time, and laboratory and pharmacy staff to manage test results and prescriptions through the same platform. The system also integrates with the university's Student Registration Portal to retrieve student information automatically. Students can view their referrals, lab results, prescriptions, and medical history through a personal dashboard.

## **1.1 Project Objectives** {#1.1-project-objectives}

1. To replace the paper-based referral process with an electronic system connecting the Student Clinic and the University Hospital.  
2. To allow clinic doctors to create, submit, and manage referrals electronically.  
3. To allow hospital doctors to receive, review, and respond to referrals through the system.  
4. To provide real-time referral status tracking for clinic staff and students.  
5. To build a centralized electronic medical record for each student, including referrals, lab results, and prescriptions.  
6. To integrate laboratory services so doctors can request tests and lab staff can enter results electronically.  
7. To connect the pharmacy so prescriptions and dispensing records are managed digitally.  
8. To integrate with the Student Registration Portal for automatic student data retrieval.

## **1.2 Scope of the Project** {#1.3-constraints}

The system is designed exclusively for use **within the University of Jordan.** It serves the Student Clinic, the University Hospital, the laboratory, the pharmacy, students, and internal administrative staff.

Students can log in to monitor their referral progress, view lab results, access prescriptions, and review their medical history. The system does not extend to external hospitals or healthcare providers outside the university.

PatientPath **does not provide online diagnosis, emergency medical services, or direct medical treatment decisions.** Instead, **it supports referral management, medical record access, lab result management, and prescription workflows within the university environment.**

## **1.3 Constraints** {#1.3-constraints}

1. **Security and Privacy:** The system handles sensitive medical data and must use encryption, secure authentication, and role-based access control.  
2. **Integration Dependency:** Connecting to the Student Registration Portal depends on API availability from the university IT department.  
3. **Internet Dependency:** The system is web-based and cannot function offline.  
4. **Academic Timeline:** The project scope is limited by the semester timeframe.  
5. **User Adoption:** Staff may need training to transition from the paper-based process.  
6. **Simulated Data:** Real patient data cannot be used; testing will use simulated records.

## **1.4 Similar Projects** {#1.4-similar-projects}

1. **ReferralMD** — [https://referralmd.com/](https://referralmd.com/) A cloud-based platform for managing patient referrals between healthcare providers. Unlike PatientPath, it targets large commercial healthcare networks.  
2. **Epic – Referral Management** — [https://www.epic.com/software/access-and-revenue-cycle/](https://www.epic.com/software/access-and-revenue-cycle/) An enterprise hospital system that manages referral workflows. It requires significant infrastructure, while PatientPath is a lightweight solution for a university setting.  
3. **Treatspace** — [https://www.treatspace.com/](https://www.treatspace.com/) A platform connecting independent providers for referral tracking. PatientPath differs by operating within a single university ecosystem with shared departments.

## **1.5 Project Organization** {#1.5-project-organization}

This report is organized into several chapters to present the PatientPath system in a clear and structured way.

**Chapter 1** provides an overview of the project, including the main idea, objectives, scope, constraints, and similar existing systems.

**Chapter 2** presents the feasibility study of the proposed system, including technical feasibility, operational feasibility, and economic feasibility.

**Chapter 3** describes the system requirements, including functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and domain requirements.

The following chapters will cover the system analysis, system design, database design, implementation details, testing process, and final conclusion.

This organization helps the reader understand the project step by step, starting from the problem and proposed solution, then moving toward the requirements, design, implementation, and evaluation of the system.

# **Chapter 2: Feasibility Study** {#chapter-2:-feasibility-study}

## **2.1 Technical Feasibility** {#2.1-technical-feasibility}

The system will be developed using the following technology stack:

* Frontend: React  
* Backend: Next.js  
* Database: PostgreSQL  
* ORM: Prisma  
* Version Control: Git & GitHub  
* UI Design: Figma

These technologies are open-source, well-documented, and widely used in modern web development. The team has prior experience working with them, and all tools are freely available. The system architecture follows a standard client-server model, which is technically achievable within the project scope.

## **2.2 Operational Feasibility** {#2.2-operational-feasibility}

The system is operationally feasible for the following reasons:

* It addresses a real and existing problem in the university clinic's referral workflow.  
* Doctors and specialists already follow similar referral steps manually, making the digital transition natural.  
* The interface will be simple, clean, and user-friendly to minimize the need for training.  
* Students gain direct access to track their referrals and view their medical records, improving their experience.

## **2.4 Legal Feasibility** {#2.4-legal-feasibility}

The proposed Digital Medical Referral System is legally feasible because it will be developed and used only within the University of Jordan environment. The system will handle sensitive medical-related information, so it must follow privacy, confidentiality, and data protection principles.

The system will not provide online diagnosis, emergency medical decisions, or direct treatment. It will only support the referral process, medical record access, lab result viewing, and prescription workflow between the Student Clinic, the University Hospital, the laboratory, and the pharmacy.

To ensure legal feasibility, the system should follow these points:

* Access to the system will be limited to authorized users only, such as students, doctors, specialists, lab staff, pharmacy staff, and administrators.  
* Each user will have permissions based on their role.  
* Students will only be able to view their own medical information and referral status.  
* Medical staff will only access the information needed to perform their work.  
* Patient data should be stored securely and not shared with any external hospital or third party.  
* The system should use secure authentication to protect user accounts.  
* The project will use simulated/test data during development and testing instead of real patient data.

Based on these conditions, the system can be considered legally feasible as long as privacy, authorization, and confidentiality rules are followed.

# **Chapter Three: System Requirements and Analysis** {#chapter-three:-system-requirements-and-analysis}

## **3.1 Stakeholders** {#3.1-stakeholders}

| Stakeholder ID | Stakeholder Name | Description |
| :---: | ----- | ----- |
| **1** | Student (Patient) | A University of Jordan student who visits the student clinic, receives medical consultations, and may be referred to the university hospital for further treatment. The student can track referral status and view updates through the system. |
| **2** | Clinic Doctor | The physician at Student Clinic who examines students, creates referrals, attaches diagnosis notes and medical reports, and monitors patient progress after referral. |
| **3** | Hospital Specialist | The specialist at the University of Jordan Hospital who receives referrals, reviews patient information, accepts or rejects referrals, schedules appointments, and submits feedback or medical summaries upon completion. |
| **4** | System Administrator | Manages user accounts, maintains system functionality, handles technical issues, configures system settings, and ensures data security and compliance with regulations. |
| **5** | Hospital Receptionist | Receives incoming referrals at the hospital side, coordinates appointment scheduling with specialists, and updates referral status in the system. |
| **6** | Lab Staff  | A laboratory technician at the University of Jordan Hospital who receives lab test requests from doctors, performs the tests, enters results into the system, and updates request statuses. Lab staff can only access laboratory-related data. |
| **7** | Pharmacy Staff  | A pharmacist at the University of Jordan Hospital who views prescriptions from doctors, dispenses medications to students, and records dispensing details in the system. Pharmacy staff can only access prescription-related data. |

#### **Table 3: Stakeholders** {#table-3:-stakeholders}

## **3.2 Data Gathering Techniques**

Two data gathering techniques were used to understand the current referral workflow, identify pain points, and collect requirements for the proposed system.

### **3.2.1 Interview** {#3.2.1-interview}

An in-person interview was conducted with Dr. Naif Abdullat at the Student Clinic) at the University of Jordan. The interview focused on understanding the current paper-based referral process, the challenges clinic staff face when communicating with the university hospital, and what features a digital system should prioritize.

Dr. Abdullat described the existing workflow: referral forms are filled manually and handed to students, who must physically deliver them to the hospital. He highlighted that this causes frequent loss of documents, long processing times, and zero visibility into whether referred students actually complete their hospital appointments. He also emphasized the need for clinic doctors to receive structured feedback from hospital specialists once a referral is completed, which does not happen under the current system.

(See Appendix A for the full interview transcript.)

### **3.2.2 Questionnaire (Survey)** {#3.2.2-questionnaire-(survey)}

An online questionnaire was distributed to University of Jordan students to evaluate their experience with the current referral process and measure their interest in a proposed electronic referral system. **A total of 68 responses** were collected. The questionnaire was divided into three sections: general background, evaluation of the current system, and evaluation of the proposed system. The full results are presented below.

**Section 1: General Background**

82.4% of respondents had visited the student clinic, and 55.9% had been referred to the university hospital 

#### The related survey results are shown in **Appendix A, Figure A.1**. {#the-related-survey-results-are-shown-in-appendix-a,-figure-a.1.}

**Section 2: Evaluating the Current Process**

Most students were dissatisfied with the current paper-based referral process, with 53% rating it 1 or 2 out of 5, and only 10.3% rating it 4 or 5 (Figure 3). The top reported problems were long processing times (75%), lost or delayed documents (35.3%), unclear referral status (33.8%), and difficulty accessing medical records (30.9%) (Figure 4). When asked whether the current system causes treatment delays, 66.2% said yes and 33.8% said sometimes. No respondent said no 

The related survey results are shown in **Appendix A, Figure A.2.**

**Section 3: Evaluating the Proposed System**

92.6% rated the proposed electronic system as very useful, and 88.2% believed it would reduce time and procedures (Figures 6–7). The most requested features were faster referrals (86.8%), easy access to medical records (70.6%), tracking student status (66.2%), and reducing paperwork (63.2%) (Figure 8). 72.1% considered it very important for the clinic doctor to view hospital treatment updates (Figure 9). Open-ended suggestions included automatic appointment scheduling, health notifications, and allowing multiple referrals per visit.

The related survey results are shown in **Appendix A, Figure A.3.**

## **3.3 Functional Requirements** {#3.3-functional-requirements}

**Priority scale: 5 \= highest, 1 \= lowest. Functional requirements are divided into 3 increments, delivered starting from increment 1\. Requirements are organized into 6 component groups(subsystem).**

**G1: Account Management**

| FR | Requirement | Description | Stakeholder | Priority | Increment |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **FR1** | Login | The user enters username and password to access the system. The system validates credentials and redirects to the role-based dashboard. | Student, Clinic Doctor, Hospital Specialist, System Administrator, Hospital Receptionist, Lab Staff, Pharmacy Staff  | 5 | 1 |
| **FR2** | Logout | The user logs out and the session is terminated. The user is redirected to the login page. | Student, Clinic Doctor, Hospital Specialist, System Administrator, Hospital Receptionist, Lab Staff, Pharmacy Staff  | 5 | 1 |
| **FR3** | Create User Account | Admin creates new user accounts and assigns roles (clinic doctor, hospital doctor, lab staff, pharmacy staff, student). | Admin | 5 | 1 |
| **FR4** | Edit User Account | Admin edits user account details such as name, role, contact information, or account status. | Admin | 4 | 2 |
| **FR5** | Deactivate User Account | Admin deactivates a user account. The user can no longer log in but their data is preserved in the system. | Admin | 4 | 2 |
| **FR6** | Reset Password | The user requests a password reset. The system sends a reset link to the registered email address.(or phone number) | Student, Clinic Doctor, Hospital Specialist, System Administrator, Hospital Receptionist, Lab Staff, Pharmacy Staff | 4 | 2 |

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

| **FR8** | View Student Profile | Displays the student's basic information retrieved from the portal. | Student, Clinic Doctor, Hospital Doctor | 5 | 1 |
| **FR9** | View Medical History | Displays the complete medical history of a student including all past referrals, lab results, prescriptions, and clinical notes. | Student, Clinic Doctor, Hospital Doctor | 5 | 1 |

## **3.4 Non-Functional Requirements** {#3.4-non-functional-requirements}

Priority scale: 5 \= highest, 1 \= lowest.

| NFR | Requirement | Description | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **NFR1** | Security | All passwords must be stored using secure hashing. No plain-text passwords. | 5 |
| **NFR2** | Security | All data transmission between client and server must use HTTPS encryption. | 5 |
| **NFR3** | Security | The system must enforce role-based access control. Each user can only access features and data relevant to their role. | 5 |
| **NFR4** | Performance | The system should load any page within 3 seconds under normal network conditions. | 4 |
| **NFR5** | Performance | The system should support at least 200 concurrent users without performance issues. | 3 |
| **NFR6** | Usability | The interface must be clean, consistent, and easy to navigate without prior training. | 4 |
| **NFR7** | Usability | The system must display clear error messages when users enter invalid data or perform unauthorized actions | 4 |
| **NFR8** | Reliability | The system should have at least 99% uptime during university working hours (8 AM – 5 PM). | 4 |
| **NFR9** | Reliability | The database must be backed up automatically on a daily basis. | 4 |
| **NFR10** | Compatibility | The system must work correctly on modern browsers: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge. | 4 |
| **NFR11** | Compatibility | The system must be responsive and usable on both desktop and mobile devices. | 3 |
| **NFR12** | Maintainability | The codebase must follow a modular architecture to allow easy future updates and feature additions. | 3 |

## **3.5 Domain Requirements** {#3.5-domain-requirements}

| DR | Description | Note |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **DR1** | Only registered University of Jordan students can have medical records in the system. | Validated through Student Registration Portal |

| **DR3** | Lab test results must follow standard medical reporting formats. | Ensures consistency |
| **DR4** | Prescriptions must include medication name, dosage, frequency, and duration. | Medical standard |

## **4.1 Class Diagram** {#4.1-class-diagram}

![][image6]

Figure 4.1: Class Diagram

**Table 12: Class Diagram Description**

| Class | Description | Attributes | Methods | Relationships |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **User** | The base class for all system users. Stores common attributes and handles authentication. All other user types inherit from this class | userId: int, username: String, password: String, email: String, role: String, isActive: boolean | login(), logout(), resetPassword() | Parent of Student, ClinicDoctor, HospitalDoctor, Admin, LabStaff, and PharmacyStaff (inheritance). Associated with Notification. |
| **Student** | Represents a university student who can view their referral status, lab results, prescriptions, and medical history. | studentId: String, name: String, faculty: String, phoneNumber: String, dateOfBirth: Date | viewProfile(), viewMedicalHistory(), trackReferralStatus() | Inherits from User. Associated with Referral (a student can have many referrals). |
| **ClinicDoctor** | Represents a doctor at the University Student Clinic who creates and submits referrals, requests lab tests, and creates prescriptions. | doctorId: String, specialization: String, department: String | createReferral(), submitReferral(), requestLabTest(), createPrescription() | Inherits from User. Associated with Referral (creates many referrals). |
| **HospitalDoctor** | Represents a specialist doctor at the Jordan University Hospital who receives, accepts or rejects referrals, updates their status, and provides feedback. | doctorId: String, specialization: String, department: String | viewIncomingReferrals(), acceptReferral(), rejectReferral(), updateReferralStatus(), addFeedback(), requestLabTest(), createPrescription() | Inherits from User. Associated with Referral (receives many referrals). |
| **Admin** | The system administrator who manages user accounts and generates system reports. | adminId: String | createUserAccount(), editUserAccount(), deactivateUserAccount(), generateReports() | Inherits from User. Associated with Report (generates many reports). |
| **LabStaff** | Represents laboratory staff who receive lab test requests and enter test results. | staffId: String, labSection: String | viewPendingRequests(), enterLabResults() | Inherits from User. Associated with LabTest (processes many lab tests). |
| **PharmacyStaff** | **Represents pharmacy staff who view prescriptions and dispense medications to students.** | **staffId: String** | **viewPrescription(), dispenseMedication()** | **Inherits from User. Associated with Prescription (dispenses many prescriptions).** |
| **Referral** | The core entity of the system. Represents a medical referral created by a clinic doctor for a student, sent to the hospital. | referralId: int, diagnosis: String, clinicalNotes: String, targetDepartment: String, status: String, createdDate: Date, updatedDate: Date, rejectionReason: String, feedback: String | create(), submit(), updateStatus(), addAttachment() | Associated with ClinicDoctor (created by one), HospitalDoctor (received by one), and Student (belongs to one). Aggregation with Attachment. Associated with LabTest and Prescription. |
| **Attachment** | Represents a file attached to a referral such as medical reports, images, or documents. | attachmentId: int, fileName: String, fileType: String, uploadDate: Date | upload(), download() | Aggregation with Referral (a referral can contain many attachments). |
| **LabTest** | Represents a laboratory test requested by a doctor for a student. Stores the test type, results, and status. | testId: int, testType: String, requestDate: Date, resultDate: Date, result: String, status: String | requestTest(), enterResult(), viewResult() | Associated with Referral (linked to one referral). Associated with LabStaff (processed by one staff member). |
| **Prescription** | Represents an electronic prescription created by a doctor. Stores medication details, dosage, and dispensing status. | prescriptionId: int, medicationName: String, dosage: String, frequency: String, duration: String, isDispensed: boolean, dispensedDate: Date | create(), dispense() | Associated with Referral (linked to one referral). Associated with PharmacyStaff (dispensed by one staff member). |
| **Notification** | Represents an in-system notification sent to users when events occur such as new referrals, status changes, or lab results. | notificationId: int, message: String, type: String, isRead: boolean, createdDate: Date | send(), markAsRead() | Associated with User (each user receives many notifications). |
| **Report** | Represents a system report generated by the admin containing statistics on referral volume, completion rates, and processing times. | reportId: int, reportType: String, generatedDate: Date, data: String | generate(), export() | Associated with Admin (generated by one admin). |

**Table 13: Class Diagram Relationship Types**

| Relationship Type | Symbol | Description | Example in PatientPath |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Inheritance** | Hollow triangle ▷ | A child class is a specialized type of the parent class. The child inherits all attributes and methods of the parent. | Student, ClinicDoctor, HospitalDoctor, Admin, LabStaff, and PharmacyStaff all inherit from User. |
| **Association** | Simple line — | A general connection between two classes indicating that they interact or are related. | ClinicDoctor creates Referral. LabStaff processes LabTest. |
| **Aggregation** | Hollow diamond ◇ | A "has-a" relationship where one class contains another, but the contained class can exist independently. | Referral contains Attachment. A referral can have attachments, but attachments could exist as standalone files. |

## **4.3 Sequence Diagrams**  {#4.3-sequence-diagrams}

| FR1 \- Login  |  |
| :---: | :---- |
| **Actors**  | **Student (Patient), Clinic Doctor, Hospital Specialist, Hospital Receptionist, System Administrator**  |
| **Description**  | **Users enter their username and password to access the system. The system validates the credentials and redirects the user to the appropriate dashboard based on their role**  |
| **Data**  | **Username , Password** |
| **Stimulus**  | **The user enters login credentials and clicks the “Login” button**  |
| **Response**  | **If the credentials are valid, the system grants access and displays the user dashboard. Otherwise, an error message is shown**  |
| **Comments**  | **Access is granted only if valid credentials are provided**  |

| :---: | :---- |

| **Description**  | **Users log out from the system. The current session is terminated securely, and the user is redirected to the login page** |
| **Data** | **User session**  |
| **Stimulus**  | **The user clicks the “Logout” button**   |
| **Response**  | **The system terminates the active session and redirects the user to the login screen successfully**   |
| **Comments**  | **All active sessions and authentication tokens must be invalidated after logout to ensure system security**  |

| **Stimulus**  | **The administrator enters the user information and clicks the “Register” button**   |

| **Stimulus**  | **The user selects a prescription record or clicks the “View Prescription” option**                      |
| **Response**  | **The system retrieves and displays the prescription information successfully**                           |

| **Stimulus**  | **The pharmacy staff selects a prescription and clicks the “Dispense Medication” button**                        |
| **Response**  | **The system updates the prescription status to dispensed and records the medication dispensing information successfully**                            |

| **Stimulus**  | **The user selects the “View Prescription History” option for a student or prescription record**                        |
| **Response**  | **The system retrieves and displays the complete prescription history successfully**                          |
